title.value: Randomized Phase II Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Semorinemab in Participants With Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer Disease: Lauriet
title.quote: Randomized Phase II Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Semorinemab in Participants With Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer Disease: Lauriet

design.value: multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 2 study with an optional open-label extension (OLE)
design.quote: The Lauriet study was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 2 study with an optional open-label extension (OLE)

population.value: Adults 50–85 years of age with mild-to-moderate AD
population.quote: Adults 50–85 years of age were eligible for participation if they: (1) met National Institute on Aging-Alzheimer's Association core clinical criteria for probable AD dementia ; (2) had a screening MMSE score of 16–21, inclusive

biomarker_confirmation.quote: centralized independent qualitative visual read of amyloid PET scan (new or prior scans) confirming the presence of cerebral amyloid pathology or CSF Aβ (1–42) ≤1,000 pg/mL

comparator.quote: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) through a centralized randomization system to 4,500 mg of semorinemab or placebo IV.

followup.quote: received 4,500 mg of IV semorinemab or placebo every 4 weeks for 48 or 60 weeks.

intervention.quote: 4,500 mg of semorinemab or placebo IV. The first 3 doses of study drug were administered biweekly to reach steady-state concentrations followed by every 4-week dosing.

outcomes.name: Change from baseline to week 49 in the ADAS-Cog11
outcomes.quote: At week 49, the semorinemab arm demonstrated a 42.2% reduction (−2.89 points, 95% CI −4.56 to −1.21, p = 0.0008) in decline on the ADAS-Cog11 (coprimary endpoint) relative to the placebo arm.
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Coprimary efficacy endpoints were change from baseline to week 49 or 61 on the 11-item version of the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale (ADAS-Cog11)

outcomes.name: Change from baseline to week 49 in the ADCS-ADL
outcomes.quote: no treatment effects were observed on the ADCS-ADL scale (coprimary endpoint; absolute difference between the 2 treatment arms in the ADCS-ADL score change from baseline of −0.83 points, 95% CI −3.39 to 1.72, p = 0.52)
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Coprimary efficacy endpoints were change from baseline to week 49 or 61 on the 11-item version of the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale (ADAS-Cog11) and the Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study-Activities of Daily Living (ADCS-ADL) scale.

outcomes.name: Change from baseline to week 49 in the CDR-SB
outcomes.quote: Change from baseline to week 49 in the CDR-SB ... 0.26 (−0.29 to 0.82) ... 0.3501
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Secondary efficacy endpoints included change from baseline on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB).

outcomes.name: Change from baseline to week 49 in the MMSE
outcomes.quote: Change from baseline to week 49 in the MMSE ... 0.27 (−0.58 to 1.11) ... 0.5366
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Secondary efficacy endpoints included change from baseline on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB).

primary_endpoint_status.quote: Based on the results of the prespecified coprimary endpoints, this study was negative.
primary_endpoint_status.explanation: The study met its coprimary endpoint for ADAS-Cog11 but failed to meet the coprimary endpoint for ADCS-ADL, rendering the overall study negative.

harms.name: vasogenic edema
harms.quote: There were no reports of vasogenic edema

harms.name: vasogenic edema
harms.quote: There were no reports of vasogenic edema

deaths.quote: Four participants died during the double-blind treatment period and/or during the safety follow-up period

discontinuations.quote: The overall discontinuation rate during the placebo-controlled treatment period (excluding safety follow-up) was 24%

limitations: The COVID-19 pandemic contributed to missed doses and/or remote or missed clinical assessments for some participants.
The relatively small sample size and lack of racial and ethnic diversity in the study cohort may also restrict the generalizability of our findings.
